subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Does the linked PR's design—stable model-visible protected schemas with authority enforced by immutable per-turn grants immediately before execution—meet OpenClaw's security boundary across embedded, MCP, Codex, Copilot, queue, compaction, fallback, and recovery paths?
rationale: Source inspection supports the separation of prompt shape from authority, but approving model visibility without executable authority is a security-boundary decision spanning multiple runtime owners and cannot be safely inferred by automation.

options.title: Accept with exact-head proof
options.body: Approve the design after focused security tests and owner review prove denied tools cannot reach hooks, implementations, remote execution, or side effects on any path.

options.title: Require hidden denied schemas
options.body: Reject the stable-catalogue design and require denied tools to remain absent from model-visible schemas despite reduced cache continuity.

options.title: Narrow the candidate
options.body: Land only the native Responses continuation portion and review the cross-runtime authorization redesign separately.

recommendation.title: Accept with exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Approve the design after focused security tests and owner review prove denied tools cannot reach hooks, implementations, remote execution, or side effects on any path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner most directly to the core agent-tool, MCP, and remote-node execution boundary requiring the decision.
